budget_tier_summary: Current budget posture is `mixed` against intended posture `medium`. Boundary-first hardware, phone-first runtime, and stripped prototype packaging keep the learning path closer to low or medium tiers, but current wireless/firmware upgrade pressure and discreet-consumer ambition still pull the project upward fast enough that alignment is weak.

where_current_direction_sits.label: Boundary-first hardware stack with minimal on-glasses compute
where_current_direction_sits.why_it_sits_here: Hardware direction is strongest when it stays simple, discreet, and package-boundary-first instead of implying tightly integrated consumer-tier hardware.
where_current_direction_sits.what_pushes_it_up: Ensure the glasses remain discreet and socially acceptable during V1 development.
where_current_direction_sits.what_could_pull_it_down: Keep scope boundary-first, phone-first, and prototype-only instead of reopening consumer-tier integration pressure.
where_current_direction_sits.tradeoff_summary: Boundary-first hardware stack with minimal on-glasses compute

where_current_direction_sits.label: Phone-first runtime over heavier autonomous on-glasses compute
where_current_direction_sits.why_it_sits_here: Software direction is currently winning when heavy compute stays off-glasses and the phone-first path is treated as the working runtime assumption.
where_current_direction_sits.what_pushes_it_up: Link-latency and reconnect evidence are still missing on the current phone-first path.
where_current_direction_sits.what_could_pull_it_down: Keep scope boundary-first, phone-first, and prototype-only instead of reopening consumer-tier integration pressure.
where_current_direction_sits.tradeoff_summary: Phone-first runtime over heavier autonomous on-glasses compute

where_current_direction_sits.label: Touch-first, lightweight display-control behavior
where_current_direction_sits.why_it_sits_here: Interaction direction is currently strongest when it stays simple, touch-first, and aligned with lightweight subtitle behavior.
where_current_direction_sits.what_pushes_it_up: Ground firmware readiness in explicit touch-input and display-control behavior instead of inferring it from project intent.
where_current_direction_sits.what_could_pull_it_down: Keep scope boundary-first, phone-first, and prototype-only instead of reopening consumer-tier integration pressure.

where_current_direction_sits.label: Subtitle-first assistive experience with conservative visible trust cues
where_current_direction_sits.why_it_sits_here: The strongest user-facing direction is still subtitle-first assistance with visible trust cues rather than broader speculative feature breadth.
where_current_direction_sits.what_pushes_it_up: Ground trust-preserving recall with confidence objects and reinforcement rules before expanding cache policy or retention scope.
where_current_direction_sits.what_could_pull_it_down: Hold the phone-first, boundary-first path and avoid adding subsystem upgrades until evidence makes them necessary.

mixed_tier_compromise_paths.label: Boundary-first main path with one evidence-justified quality upgrade at a time
mixed_tier_compromise_paths.why_it_sits_here: Keep the current low-tier boundary package as the base and add at most one subsystem quality-upgrade package only after stronger evidence appears.

mixed_tier_compromise_paths.what_could_pull_it_down: Stage subsystem upgrades one at a time after link or firmware evidence removes guesswork.
mixed_tier_compromise_paths.tradeoff_summary: This preserves prototype buildability while reducing unnecessary upward drift, but it still does not make the discreet consumer tier credible.

tier_pressure_points: Intended budget posture is `medium`, but the current project posture reads `mixed` under target tier `discreet_consumer_assistive_wearable`.
Wireless and firmware quality-upgrade pressure are the clearest current upward-drift drivers.
Boundary-first hardware and phone-first runtime are the clearest current cost-down anchors.
As a prototype-learning path this can still be worthwhile, but for a discreet consumer product target the current direction is economically weak enough that it should be stopped or reframed unless...
what_is_pushing_cost_up: A discreet consumer-wearable posture pushes miniaturization, packaging, and industrial-design pressure before cost credibility is proven.
Current component posture is only subsystem-BOM-level, which is enough to see packaging pressure but not enough to support a consumer-tier cost story.
Wireless posture is still `needs_attention` / `limited_evidence`, so radio, battery, and reconnect behavior still carry economic risk.
Firmware posture is still `needs_attention` / `limited_evidence`, so touch-input and display-control simplicity may cost more than the prototype framing suggests.
what_is_keeping_cost_down: Hardware simplicity is the strongest grounded lane, so boundary-first packaging beats heavier integrated hardware assumptions.
Phone-first runtime currently fits cost, thermal, battery, and discreetness pressure better than autonomous glasses compute.
Touch-first and lightweight display behavior fit the current firmware and trust posture better than richer interaction assumptions.

what_would_realign_the_project: Keep the main path prototype-only and stop treating the current architecture as a discreet consumer product path while cost posture stays harsh.
Use the boundary-first hardware package as the base and add quality-upgrade packages only after evidence justifies them.
Capture wireless link and firmware behavior evidence before hardening medium or ambitious subsystem commitments.
If the discreet consumer tier still matters, tighten operator intent or reframe the target tier before more product-shaped work accumulates.
prototype_vs_product_budget_note: A lower-tier or mixed-tier prototype-learning path can still be worthwhile, but the same posture does not make the current discreet consumer product ambition credible. Prototype budget fit and product budget fit must stay separate.
